title: TGFBI Corneal Dystrophies: Granular (GCD1) & Avellino (GCD2)
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to the 5q31-linked TGFBI dystrophies. These conditions involve the progressive accumulation of hyaline and amyloid deposits in the corneal stroma, leading to vision loss and recurrent erosions.

sections.title: GCD1 vs. GCD2: A Comparative Analysis

rows: Granular dots + Lattice-like lines + Star-shaped opacities
Gradual decline; severe in later life

sections.title: Etiology & Pathophysiology
sections.content: The TGFBI gene encodes keratoepithelin, a 68-kDa extracellular matrix protein. Mutations lead to misfolding and accumulation of insoluble mutant protein. In GCD1, the Arg555Trp mutation causes purely hyaline deposits. In GCD2 (Avellino), the Arg124His mutation results in a unique phenotypic mix of hyaline (granular) and amyloid (lattice-like) features. Deposits typically begin in the anterior stroma and progress posteriorly and peripherally.

sections.title: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION
content: NEVER perform LASIK or PRK on patients with Granular/Avellino Dystrophy.
Laser refractive surgery triggers a massive wound-healing response.
Results in catastrophic, rapid deposition of mutant protein across the interface.
Genetic screening is mandatory in high-prevalence regions (e.g., Korea) before refractive surgery.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workflow
content: Step 1: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy (Sclerotic scatter is key).
Step 2: Anterior Segment OCT (Hyper-reflective stromal deposits).
Step 3: Genetic Testing (Confirms TGFBI mutation; Gold Standard).
Step 4: IVCM (In Vivo Confocal Microscopy) for deposit depth.
Step 5: Histopathology (Masson Trichrome and Congo Red stains).

content.mnemonic: Marilyn Monroe Always Gets Her Men in Sunny Cinema
content.explanation: M-Macular: M-Masson Trichrome/Acid-Schiff (False: Macular is Alcian Blue); G-Granular: H-Hyaline (Masson Trichrome); L-Lattice: A-Amyloid (Congo Red). Focus: Granular = Red (Masson); Lattice = Green (Congo Red bifringence).

sections.title: Management Ladder
content: 1. Conservative: Lubrication and bandage contact lenses (BCL) for RCEs.
2. PTK (Phototherapeutic Keratectomy): For superficial deposits and RCE management.
3. DALK (Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty): Preferred over PKP if endothelium is healthy.
4. PKP (Penetrating Keratoplasty): For full-thickness stromal involvement.
5. Post-Op: Monitor for recurrence in the graft (very common).

rows: Well-defined, mapped mutation; strong clinical evidence.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: GCD1: Clear spaces between 'crumbs' remain clear until late stages.
GCD2: Amyloid lines are typically fewer and thicker than in Lattice Dystrophy Type 1.
Recurrence: In GCD, recurrence in grafts often appears as a superficial subepithelial haze first.
Homozygotes: Rare, but present with much earlier and more aggressive disease than heterozygotes.

sections.title: Recent Advances
content: Gene Silencing: siRNA-based therapies aiming to reduce mutant TGFBI mRNA.
CRISPR/Cas9: Research into allele-specific gene editing to 'turn off' the mutant allele.
Autophagy Modulators: Investigating drugs that enhance the clearance of misfolded proteins.
Universal Pre-Refractive Genetic Screening: Becoming standard in high-risk populations.

sections.title: Surgical Complications
content: Graft Recurrence: Almost 100% over 15-20 years.
Iatrogenic Ectasia: Risk if PTK is too aggressive.
Interface Opacification: Unique to lamellar procedures.
Steroid-Induced Glaucoma: Post-keratoplasty risk.

sections.title: Investigation: OCT Interpretation
sections.content: Anterior Segment OCT (AS-OCT) is vital for surgical planning. Deposits in GCD appear as highly reflective 'shards' within the stroma. AS-OCT helps differentiate if deposits are limited to the anterior 100-150 microns (suitable for PTK) or extend deeper (requiring DALK/PKP).
